item.title: David Warner starts fresh Sandpapergate row after Graeme Hick rejects Khawaja's dressing-room claims
item.description: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick and David Warner. While Hick has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper, Warner has hit back at the former coach, questioning his appointment and bringing Michael Di Venuto into the debate. What did Graeme Hick say about Khawaja's claims? Hick, who was part of Australia's coaching staff during the 2018 South Africa tour, described Khawaja's allegations as "absolutely false". He maintained that he had no knowledge of any discussions about using sandpaper and only became aware of the incident after seeing the footage on the big screen in Cape Town. Khawaja had claimed that the entire dressing room was aware of the ball-tampering, suggesting that responsibility for the incident went beyond the three players who were eventually punished. Warner responded by taking aim at Hick's appointment as Australia's batting coach, bringing former assistant coach Michael Di Venuto into the discussion. In response to an X post on the interview, Warner wrote: "Let's get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved. As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him. These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!" — davidwarner31 (@davidwarner31) Why has the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced? The latest exchange follows the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, in which the Australia batter revisited the events of the 2018 South Africa tour. His account has reopened questions about how much the dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident and whether the original investigation captured the full extent of what happened. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball using a piece of sandpaper. The incident became known as Sandpapergate and led to major sanctions against the players involved. Warner and then Australia captain Steve Smith were handed one-year suspensions by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban. The episode also led to widespread criticism of Australian cricket and prompted questions about the team's culture and leadership.

item.title: 2027 Masters: Austin Smotherman still fighting for Augusta invite despite back-to-back fall wins
item.description: What a year 2026 has been for Austin Smotherman. He welcomed his third daughter into the world after contending at the Cognizant Classic this winter . He made his first major championship start at Aronimink a few months later. Not discouraged from the missed cut at the PGA Championship, the 32-year-old Smotherman won for the first time in his 100th start on Tour at the Bank of Utah Championship. He didn't let the time between career win No. 1 and No. 2 last very long. Three weeks later in Bermuda, Smotherman stood in the winner’s circle again after ousting Seamus Power in a two-man playoff after weather cut the tournament short to 54 holes. With all that, his playing status secured through 2029. And now, one more mountain to climb: Finish inside the top 50 of the Official World Golf Ranking. If he clinches that before the end of the season, the No. 51-ranked Smotherman will get his first-ever invite to Augusta National. There's some risk involved — two missed cuts could theoretically send him down, outside the top 60 in the FedExCup fall points and lose his spot in the first two signature events of 2027. It's a bet Smotherman is willing to take considering the possible reward. "Do our best to put up good weeks and earn some more World Ranking points and cap off the fall hopefully on a high note," he said at his press conference at this week’s Austin Championship when asked about his plan for the next couple of weeks. "Can't take away what we did," Smotherman added. "If we miss two cuts coming up, still doing a lot well and it was the best decision I think to go give it a run. The world ranking points system, I don't understand it perfectly, that's for my team to tell me what's going on. I'm just going to go play golf." Smotherman, who turned pro in 2016 and played in Latin America the following year, credited the experience from traveling the world for helping him land where he is ahead of the season-finale tournament in Georgia next week. "I feel like my good's been good enough to have a chance to win out here for a long time," the back-to-back winner said. "I made a bunch of cuts, I've had stretches of a lot of missed cuts, I feel like I've done everything in between," he added. "So to cap off wins now is a different feeling kind of getting that under my belt." item.description: USC players celebrate a made basket during a Big Ten college basketball game against the College of Charleston, Tuesday, November 10, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES –– Perfection is cruel, and Sitaya Fagan is learning the harsh reality of excellence. Fagan checked out of the game with minutes left in the fourth quarter, plopped into her chair, and cried. USC led 101-44. 57 points. The USC Trojans defeated the Charleston Cougars 105-44, but the story rests in the palms that held the face of the woman who went 0-for-7. The boulder-sized lump sat in her throat and chest, heavy and immovable, refusing to accept the scoreboard's narrative. Perfection is the culmination of habits amalgamated when nobody's watching. Intensity. Focus. Dedication. Efficiency. This is what USC is building. Jazzy Davidson found Fagan first, wrapped an arm around her and whispered in her ear. I've been there," Davidson said later. "We expect greatness out of all of us and being a perfectionist—it makes her who she is, but there's also a downside to that." The downside. The stone. The tears after a blowout. If you want to understand this USC team, start there. Start with a kid from Australia, miles away from the comforts of home, family and friends, crying over missed shots in a game her team led by 35 at halftime. Start with the feeling that her nine rebounds, three blocks, and two steals meant nothing because the ball wouldn't go through the net. That's not weakness. That's the obverse of the same coin that has Davidson shooting 75% on the season. It's fanatical. It's almost grandiloquent in its devotion. It's the kind of maniacal obsession that either makes championships or breaks them. In Greek mythology, three sisters controlled the threads of life. Clotho spun it. Lachesis measured it. item.title: Oregon's Lanning delivers KO response to Michigan's Whittingham
item.description: Two days after Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said that Oregon coach Dan Lanning has “$50-plus million” to build a football, Lanning responded with a dig. Lanning 1, Whittingham 0. The coaches will face each other on Saturday, Nov. 14, when Michigan plays at Oregon’s Autzen Stadium. Michigan is 5-4, 2-4 Big Ten, while Oregon is 6-3, 4-2. “Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach,” Whittingham said Monday, Nov. 9, on the “Inside Michigan Football” radio show, referring to Lanning. “Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting. It doesn’t hurt that you have $50-plus million at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. That’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. “NIL is really the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much. It used to be the facilities you had, the tradition, all these other things. And now it’s, ‘Well, this is all great. But these guys have got 100 grand more for me.’ So, that’s a little bit of a factor to say the least. Not to take anything away from Dan because he is an outstanding recruiter.” Michigan reportedly has a budget of $40 million for its roster. Lanning, at his news conference on Wednesday, Nov. 11, was asked about Whittingham’s comments regarding Oregon’s budget. "Man, I've got nothing to say to Coach Whitt other than I think he's an unbelievable coach," Lanning told reporters. “And I get it — they're spending more money on the coaches they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players, but I know they've signed a couple guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player, I don't know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He's a Hall of Fame coach. I've got nothing but respect for him." Lanning’s not-so-subtle reference was to Whittingham’s firing of offensive coordinator Jason Beck last Sunday, Nov. 8 after nine games. Michigan owes Beck nearly $10 million after being fired in the first-year of a three-year contract. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Nate Danielson Responds Right Away After Red Wings Demotion
item.description: Three days after the Detroit Red Wings sent him down , Nate Danielson made the most of his first game back in the AHL. The 22-year-old center recorded three assists in the Grand Rapids Griffins’ 6-3 win over the Rockford IceHogs on Wednesday morning, his first game of the season with Grand Rapids. Two of those assists went to John Leonard, who scored in all three periods for the hat trick in his own first game back with the Griffins. The other set up Axel Sandin-Pellikka’s power-play goal in the first period. Carter Bear added two goals and two assists, and Grand Rapids moved to 11-2-1-1 with 24 points . Nov 5, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings center Nate Danielson (29) skates with the puck in the second period against the Vegas Golden Knights at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Why the Red Wings sent Nate Danielson down Danielson played 13 games with Detroit this season without scoring a goal, finishing that stretch with two assists and a minus-5 rating. He was a healthy scratch for Saturday’s 4-0 loss at Colorado, and the Red Wings reassigned him to Grand Rapids on Sunday along with goaltender Michal Postava and Leonard. Red Wings coach Todd McLellan, speaking to reporters in comments published by Detroit Hockey Now , said the 2023 first-rounder is getting closer to what the staff wants. “I guess that energy gauge is starting to come closer to the middle, I think, for Danny,” McLellan said. “If he can push it over the top, I think he’s got all the tools.” What Nate Danielson said after the win Wednesday’s game was a School Day matinee at Van Andel Arena, the morning start the Griffins play in front of busloads of students. Grand Rapids has now won four of those in a row. Danielson spoke with reporters afterward and said he enjoys the early puck drop, in a video posted by the Hockeytown West Podcast : “I think they’re fun, it kind of reminds you of when you were a kid you just get up and go play.” What it takes to earn the call back up Danielson was the ninth overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NHL Draft and has played 41 NHL games in his career. A longer look in Grand Rapids may do more for him than the in-and-out role he had in Detroit. The Griffins are 11-2-1-1. The Red Wings have lost four straight and sit at 7-9-3 after Tuesday’s 3-2 loss in St. Louis. The truth is that he might be in a better spot for his development on a winning team than on a Detroit team that keeps losing. If he keeps filling the scoresheet the way he did Wednesday, the trip back up will not take long.

item.title: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit
item.description: LAS VEGAS – The Cincinnati Reds ' impossible-dream offseason just got a lot tougher with the Detroit Tigers ' $11.5 million signing of free agent Reds closer Emilio Pagán . The one-year agreement, which comes three weeks before an anticipated MLB labor lockout, also includes a bonus package. Until the deal was struck, the Reds were keeping in touch with Pagán for a possible return since declining a $10 million option for 2027 less than two weeks ago. Manager Terry Francona said as recently as Nov. 6 during a radio interview that he held out hope that Pagán would return. Pagán, 35, converted all 19 save chances with a 1.88 ERA after returning from a severe hamstring injury for the final three months of the season. He became the Reds' closer in April 2025 and earned a career-high 32 saves with a 2.88 ERA on the way to the playoffs that year. “I loved having him. He was great,” team president Nick Krall said of the veteran who was valued almost as much for his clubhouse influence as his high-level performance on the mound. “He’s been really good for us the last three, four years.” One of the reasons a return seemed plausible when Pagán opted out of his Reds contract was that he returned as a free agent a year ago after his original two-year, $16 million deal with the Reds expired. Both sides said the door was open to return and continued a dialogue. The Reds went from that playoff berth in 2025 to last place this year, their hitters striking out more and scoring less than anyone else in the league, their pitchers walking more than anyone else and their fielding ranking among the worst in the majors. Now they have to add a closer to a laundry list of needs to fill to have any semblance of a chance to return to the playoffs – which they continue to say is their goal. Krall looks like he's working without a net in that effort. He's definitely working without a payroll budget, which he said has not been determined as he spoke in Las Vegas this week during MLB's annual GM meetings. So where does all of that put the Reds’ thinking when it comes to the enormous ninth-inning hole in their pitching staff? Try to fill it specifically with an acquisition during an uncertain winter? Throw a bunch of arms into a spring competition and see where it lands? “Obviously you’d love to build the bullpen from the back forward,” Krall said. “But it’s something we’re just going to work through this offseason, and we’ll do the best we can.” This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit

item.title: 'I wasn't in that dressing room': Joe Root reacts to Usman Khawaja's fresh Sandpapergate revelations
item.description: NEW DELHI: England Test captain Joe Root has chosen not to comment on the fresh allegations surrounding Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as 'Sandpapergate'. Speaking ahead of England's three-match ODI series against Australia, Root said he did not know what had happened inside the Australian dressing room and wanted to concentrate on the matches ahead. "I wasn't in that [Australia] dressing room, I don't know what went on. I don't want to speculate. My focus is with this team right now and what we've got coming up," Root said. He added that England had no clear information about the latest claims and wanted to focus on the ODI series. When asked whether he had experienced similar practices in cricket, Root said, "I can only speak from my own experiences and that's not how I feel, no." Khawaja's fresh claims reopen Sandpapergate The controversy has returned to the spotlight following revelations in former Australian batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr. Khawaja claimed that ball-tampering was not limited to Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, suggesting that the wider Australian team, including support staff, knew about the practice. He also alleged that Australia had been lifting the ball's quarter seam during the 2017-18 Ashes series to help generate reverse swing. Khawaja believes the three players should not be left carrying the blame alone and has called for collective responsibility. The original scandal took place during the 2018 Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Smith and Warner received one-year bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months after being caught using sandpaper on the ball. Handscomb also avoids fresh comments Australian batter Peter Handscomb, who was part of the squad during the Cape Town Test, also declined to discuss Khawaja's claims. "Look, I appreciate you have to ask these questions. I've had a nice day today, and it's not really something that I want to comment on right now. I'll sort of just let the powers of people do their thing,” he said. Handscomb added that players must learn to move forward despite off-field controversies and outside discussions.

item.description: Ousted ESPN voice accuses network of ‘push’ to make Troy Aikman the ‘bad guy’ in Joe Buck feud originally appeared on The Sporting News . The two have a long partnership, and have been working together for 25 seasons in a row. While they have been working together for decades, their partnership is now in danger with a recent argument between the two. Another famous personality has now given his opinion on the matter. Ryan Clark criticizes ESPN for treating Troy Aikman harshly Former ESPN analyst Ryan Clark has accused ESPN of deliberately framing the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback as the villain in the ongoing contract dispute involving Buck. On a recent episode of “The Pivot” podcast, Clark described the pair’s 25-year partnership. He said, “It felt like brothers, it felt like family. Somebody is trying to make Troy Aikman look like the bastard son. You mention the leaks, I’ve been around there. I know how it starts to happen when they’re trying to build a narrative about you. I’ve been around there. I know what it is when they’ll have your back and support you through anything.. even when you’re wrong, when they’ll come out and make a statement, ‘we’re fully behind this guy.’ They haven’t done that for Troy.” He added, “So I do feel like there’s a push to make him be the bad guy, whether he is or not. I know that they have ways of maneuvering to protect humans. And I know they have ways of putting people in positions where a narrative is built around them, so when they make their exit, they can seem like the good guys. Because I was a part of that.” Clark further said that there is a business side to the feud, “Contract negotiations happen… This is not about Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. This is about business. And it’s about business being done dirty.” Clark was himself fired by the network back in July, and learned about it during an appearance on “NFL Live.” Buck signed a six-year extension with ESPN in September 2026 reportedly worth about $108 million, or roughly $18 million annually. Aikman’s five-year deal, valued near $90 million when signed in 2022, expires after the network’s first Super Bowl broadcast on February 14, 2027. Aikman has not received a comparable offer, and negotiations have stalled. This has created friction in the pair’s relationship. The two reportedly argued in the booth before the October 12 Buffalo Bills – Los Angeles Rams game.
